I found one bug in the uncommitted changes, at `billing/invoice.py:19`.

`billable_hours` computes `(session.end - session.start).total_seconds()`. Both datetimes are in the account's time zone and share the same `ZoneInfo` object. In that case Python subtracts the wall-clock times and ignores the UTC offset. A session that spans a DST change therefore gets the wrong duration.

- **Spring forward:** an a-100 session from 01:30 EST to 03:30 EDT on 2026-03-08 lasts 1 real hour but computes as 2. That is an overcharge.
- **Fall back:** a session that really lasts 2h30m can compute as 1h30m, which rounds up to 2 billed hours instead of 3. That is an undercharge. A real 1h session can compute as 0, and `max(1, ...)` then hides it.

The fix is to convert both timestamps to UTC before subtracting, for example `end.astimezone(timezone.utc) - start.astimezone(timezone.utc)`.

I found this by reading the code and checking `billing/clock.py` and `billing/sessions.py`. I didn't run the tests. The new tests only use July dates, so they wouldn't catch it. I haven't changed anything.

input.command: cat billing/accounts.py billing/sessions.py; sed -n 30,60p billing/invoice.py; sed -n 1,20p tests/test_invoice.py

findings.summary: billable_hours subtracts two aware datetimes that share the same ZoneInfo, so Python does wall-clock subtraction and ignores the UTC offset; sessions that span a DST change get the wrong duration.
findings.failure_scenario: An a-100 (America/New_York) session runs from 2026-03-08 01:30 EST to 03:30 EDT. That is 1 real hour (06:30Z to 07:30Z). The wall-clock difference is 2h, so it is billed as 2 hours instead of 1, an overcharge. On the fall-back night (2026-11-01, 01:30 EDT to 01:30 EST) the real 1h is computed as 0, then clamped to 1 by max(1, ...). A 2h30m real session can be billed as 1h30m, which rounds up to 2 hours instead of 3, an undercharge. Sessions.py stores start and end already converted to local time, so the real elapsed time has to be computed after converting both back to UTC, e.g. (end.astimezone(timezone.utc) - start.astimezone(timezone.utc)). The new tests only use July dates, so they miss this.
findings.short_summary: Duration ignores UTC offset across DST transitions
